It takes no institutional stance and is advisory.

documents.title: Student Conduct
documents.summary: The Dean of Students conduct page describes the Student Code of Conduct process. AI appears only twice: prohibited AI tools count as academic dishonesty, and students are told to read each syllabus because instructors set different AI limits.

documents.summary: A knowledge-base article from the Center for Teaching & Learning with three ready-to-paste syllabus statements: AI prohibited, AI only with prior instructor permission, and AI allowed with citation and a short note. Each ties violations to the Student Code of Conduct.

documents.title: Teaching Guide: AI Writing Tools
tiers: Example statement prohibiting the use of AI writing tools
Example statement permitting limited use of AI writing tools
Example statement permitting all use of AI writing tools

documents.title: Statement on Responsible and Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Short IT-office statement on responsible and acceptable AI use at UIC. It states principles, data-handling duties for sensitive data and a note that guidance will change, and points to U of I System student and instructor guidance for classroom rules.

documents.title: Generative AI resources and guidance for faculty
documents.summary: Provost and Health Affairs letter to faculty from September 2023 reminding them of System and campus generative AI guidance. It encourages responsible use, repeats the sensitive-data ticket rule, and points to CATE syllabus statements and workshops.

documents.title: Graduate Degree Requirements, Department of Computer Science, 2025
documents.summary: Graduate handbook of the CS department, graduate students only. Two short passages allow generative AI for improving writing, keep the student responsible, allow class-level restrictions, and require a pre-AI draft for the WCP critique.

documents.title: Graduate Degree Requirements, Department of Computer Science, 2023
documents.summary: Earlier edition (2023) of the CS graduate handbook, graduate students only. It bans AI writing tools and paraphrasing software unless explicitly allowed, exempts spell-checkers, and tells students to ask when in doubt. The 2025 edition relaxed this.

name: Illinois Institute of Technology
notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Three university-layer documents coded (CTS Generative AI Policy, CTS Guidelines for AI Applications, CLI AI for Teaching and Learning); the 2023 Faculty Guide was screened out. The two CTS documents mostly bind faculty and staff on data and security, with few student coursework rules. The CLI syllabus statements are suggested templates, coded as written but not binding rules. No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred.

documents.title: AI for Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: Center for Learning Innovation page presenting faculty support and suggested syllabus statements at three levels of AI use plus an AI-and-assessment statement for instructors. It asks faculty to state AI expectations in their syllabi and describes AI workshops. The sample language includes a 25% cap on AI content and citation requirements.

documents.title: Generative AI Policy (v1.0)
documents.summary: Version 1.0 university policy from CTS setting core requirements for lawful, ethical use of AI by faculty, staff, students and affiliates. Its rules mostly bind faculty and staff and cover compliance, attribution, output review, bias, security review, data ownership and IP. It says nothing about student coursework rules.

documents.title: Guidelines for AI Applications in Academic and Administrative Work (v1.0)
documents.summary: CTS guidelines for students, staff and faculty on AI applications. They name Microsoft Copilot as the supported tool, steer users away from other tools for institutional data, and set best practices for data protection, integrity, disclosure and verification. Violations go to the Acceptable Use Policy; review is annual.

name: Illinois State University
notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. School and computing layers none found; course layer deferred. One A-only unit dropped: the top-of-page sentence that invented or poorly cited references are the easiest evidence of AI content, a near-repeat of the Crossref/hallucination unit that both coders coded. CIPD syllabus-statement units use P09 as a loose fit (a suggested, not required, statement); no UNCOVERED units remained. CIPD stance is restrict (default ban conditional on instructor authorization); a delegates reading is arguable. Missed by both coders and not added: Graduate School sentence 'It is vital that students uphold the core principles of academic and research integrity'.

documents.title: Generative AI in the Classroom
documents.summary: Teaching-center guide applying the Student Code of Conduct to AI: unauthorized or uncited AI use is an integrity violation, detectors are not recommended, and instructors get assignment-design ideas to discourage or incorporate AI. It also points to syllabus language and consultation.

documents.title: Ethical Use of Generative AI (thesis, dissertation, capstone, comprehensive exams)
documents.summary: Graduate School statement on generative AI in culminating work. It requires disclosure to the committee and citation, ties unauthorized use to Policy 1.8, and lets units add rules.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) at ISU
documents.summary: IT help page listing campus AI tools and a ban on entering restricted data into Copilot, plus pointers to the responsible-AI committee and evolving standards. Little teaching policy.

name: Indiana University Indianapolis
notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Two university-layer teaching-center documents only; no school or computing documents were found and course syllabi were deferred. The Teaching.IU sample syllabus statements are IU Bloomington FACET templates, coded as stated offerings and not as binding IU rules. Two UNCOVERED units remain in the CTL FAQ (proactive not punitive approach; clarifying assignment purpose). The kb.iu.edu acceptable-use page was inaccessible.

documents.unit: Center for Teaching and Learning, IU Indianapolis
documents.title: Generative AI in the Classroom FAQs
documents.summary: Campus teaching-center FAQ for faculty. It reports Copilot as the only approved tool for internal data, advises against detectors, and recommends a learner-centered, non-punitive approach. It sets no student rule and leaves syllabus policy to instructors and departments.

documents.title: Policies and Guidance: Generative AI
documents.summary: IU system-wide teaching page saying IU has no AI-specific policy beyond data security, naming Copilot as preferred tool, and pointing to existing misconduct rules. It offers two sample syllabus statements (open and strict) and advice from an IU Bloomington professor on communicating and framing AI policy.

name: Indiana University of Pennsylvania
notes: Thin source: one AI sentence plus the AI mention in the plagiarism definition. Reconciled from coders A and B.

documents.title: Types of Violations (Academic Integrity Policy, incl. AI-Generated Work)
documents.summary: IUP's academic integrity page defines violation types; its only AI content is that plagiarism covers AI-generated sources and that AI-generated work is unacceptable unless the instructor or administrator authorizes it.

name: Iowa State University
notes: Single included document (Office of Student Conduct faculty page); only AI-related passages coded. CELT syllabus-options page not resolved in collection. One UNCOVERED unit (evidence basis for judging AI concerns).

documents.unit: Office of Student Conduct (Dean of Students Office)
documents.title: Know the Code Resources: Faculty and Staff (Artificial Intelligence section)
documents.summary: The Office of Student Conduct's faculty page has a short AI section that treats generative AI as permitted, restricted or prohibited depending on the course, assignment or instructor. It urges instructors to state expectations, discuss them, design assignments that show student process, and not rely on AI detectors alone, and it points to CELT syllabus language and sample statements.

name: University of Iowa
notes: Merged from coders A and B (A: 171 units, B: 108). Computing layer none-found and course layer deferred per the collect file. Topic codes are mapped to the starter codebook in tools/AGENT_BRIEF.md (coder A had used free labels). Sample syllabus language in the Teaching With AI page is coded as templates offered to instructors, not Iowa rules (fit notes say where they come from). The CLAS memo's sanctions and reporting rules (P37, P80, P81, P64) are general academic-misconduct rules, coded because the memo is the college's AI-misconduct guidance. Units dropped after checking the source: student-expectations 'could result in serious academic consequences' (same sentence as the P36 unit; A's fit note: warns of unspecified serious consequences, P37 needs concrete penalties) and 'AI is a rapidly developing technology' (A P54, fit note: only notes that guidance will change, promises no review; it is the reason clause of the P102 sentence); OTLT article: 'If you choose to set limits around student AI use' (condition of the misconduct-language sentence), 'avoid unintentional academic misconduct' (rationale clause, covered by the closing P99 unit), the list of external disclosure style guides (links only), and the scene-setting sentence 'Generative AI tools are reshaping how students study, write, and learn' (A UNCOVERED, note: scene-setting statement with no rule attached; not a policy); Teaching With AI page: 'hiring a person or a company to write essays' (sample-template wording not about AI), the detector reading list, the Gradescope sentence (grading tool, not about AI) and the pointer to the chatbot guidance page (navigation). Fit notes of the last two dropped units: detector reading list (cites research on detector accuracy, not on how AI affects learning) and Gradescope (mentions paper-based tests as an option; no shift in weight is stated).

documents.title: Student Expectations (Using AI Responsibly)
documents.summary: Student-facing page stating that Iowa has no single university-wide AI policy and that expectations vary by instructor, assignment, department and college. It lists student responsibilities and ties unauthorized AI use to the Academic Misconduct Policy.

documents.title: Teaching With AI
tiers: Low / Moderate / High risk categories for instructor AI use cases
documents.summary: Instructor-facing page on teaching with AI: recommended tools and use cases, risk-rated Q&A on instructor uses, syllabus sample language for prohibit, attribute and encourage options, and advice on detectors, assessment design, AI browsers and smart glasses. It sets no student default and tells instructors to set clear expectations.

documents.unit: Office of Teaching, Learning, and Technology
documents.title: Teaching with AI: Setting Expectations in Your Syllabus
tiers: AI Assessment Scale (Perkins & Furze), suggested to instructors as a shared framework
documents.summary: Teaching-office article urging instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, repeat them in each assignment, and explain how students should cite or disclose AI use. It offers task-by-task examples, the AI Assessment Scale and a sample disclosure statement.

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice President and Provost
documents.title: Artificial intelligence guidance for instructors
documents.summary: A Spring 2024 email from the Provost's office and the CIO asking instructors to communicate their own AI policy to students in the first week. It lists faculty resources, Copilot and training opportunities.

documents.unit: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (contains Computer Science)
documents.title: Reminder of CLAS guidelines for handling academic misconduct (AI Q&A)
documents.summary: A CLAS memo on handling undergraduate academic misconduct, with one Q&A on written work that appears AI-generated. It tells instructors to follow their syllabus policy, otherwise to meet the student, and notes that Turnitin does not reliably flag AI text.

name: Jackson State University
notes: Only the AI Policy section of the common syllabus page was coded; the Academic Honesty text above it does not mention AI. No separate provost, college or computing policy found. Both coders found the same 20 units; the list-item permissions were normalized to include the 'with instructor approval' lead-in.

documents.unit: THEE Pathway (General Education) common syllabus links
documents.title: Common Syllabus Links for Students: AI Policy
documents.summary: A short university AI statement in the common syllabus text: AI is allowed for listed tasks only with instructor approval, fully AI-created graded work is barred and may earn a zero, and AI use must be cited. It also bars entering confidential data into AI, and lets faculty add their own criteria.

name: James Madison University
notes: Consensus of coders A and B. Two university-layer documents (IT standard on AI with university data; library guide on syllabus statements). Course layer deferred; no school or computing documents found. The IT standard governs university data and tools rather than classroom work, so most units are P50/P56. The DeepSeek ban is UNCOVERED (named-tool ban; no new type proposed, one unit). The library guide dates a cited MIT report as August 2026, as in the source. The guide is advice to instructors, not an enforceable policy.

documents.title: Standard for Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence with University Data
documents.summary: An IT standard for all JMU faculty, staff and students on using AI with university data. It names Copilot Chat as the only approved GenAI tool, requires review for others, sets data-protection and disclosure duties, and lists risks. It does not set classroom rules and points to separate AI in Education guidance.

documents.unit: JMU Libraries (with Center for Faculty Innovation)
documents.title: Academic Integrity, Syllabi Statements and AI (Artificial Intelligence in Education guide)
documents.summary: A library research guide that advises instructors how to write syllabus statements and set AI expectations assignment by assignment using a five-level scale. It recommends against AI detectors and for process evidence. It is advice, not an enforceable policy.

name: Johns Hopkins University
notes: Reconciled: both coders coded zero documents because every JHU page (university guidelines, genai.jhu.edu, WSE pages) was blocked (Cloudflare/403) at collection. No documents coded: the collect file has no documents with screen=include (JHU pages were blocked/inaccessible). No document collected. The JHU university-wide 'Guidelines for the Responsible Use of AI' (IT@JH; mirrored at https://ladacademy.facultyaffairs.jhu.edu/resources/guidelines-for-the-responsible-use-of-ai), the genai.jhu.edu pages, and the Whiting School of Engineering pages (https://wseit.engineering.jhu.edu/get-help/generative-ai-chatgpt-information, https://engineering.jhu.edu/ctld/chatgpt/) all return a Cloudflare 'Sorry, you have been blocked' page to curl (fetch_text.py) and HTTP 403 to WebFetch; the Wayback Machine has no copy. The support.cmts.jhu.edu WSE 'Responsible Use of AI Tools at WSE' page fetched empty. Search snippets (not verbatim text) say the university guidelines defer to existing codes of conduct and academic integrity policies and tell students to consult instructors before using GenAI in coursework. No JHU CS department-level AI policy was found; the only known URL (cs220 syllabus) is a course document and is deferred. Retry from a different network or a browser-capable fetch route.

name: Kansas State University
notes: Three university-layer documents (TLC sample syllabus language, a draft employee records/GenAI policy, and the provost task-force page); no school, computing or course layer collected. Reconciled from coders A and B.

documents.title: Using Generative AI with University Owned Records and Data Policy
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); date not stated in extracted text
documents.summary: An unnumbered draft policy ('Chapter ????') on employees' and contractors' use of generative AI with university records and data. It allows AI with conditions on protected data, vetted tools, human review and disclosure, sets sanctions, and calls for annual updates. It does not address students' coursework use of AI.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (Responsible Use of Generative AI Task Force)
documents.summary: Provost's page describing a task force charged with building a university AI framework: its focus areas, key activities, members and working groups. It states no rules for students; the policy is still being developed.

documents.title: Sample AI Policy Language
tiers: AI Permitted (version 1: cite; version 2: 150-300 word AI Acknowledgement)
AI Required (version 1: transparent use; version 2: co-created class agreement)
documents.summary: TLC page of sample syllabus statements, compiled from Western Michigan and Oklahoma State, that K-State instructors can adapt. It offers three levels (prohibited, permitted, required), all with citation and a tie to the K-State Honor Pledge. It is model language, not a binding university rule.

name: University of Kansas
notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Disagreements were mostly: (1) phase for the ask-when-unsure rule (P10) and for informs statements, set to during-work and general; (2) actor all versus a named role; (3) unit_stance for disclosure duties, where 'require' was reserved for AI use itself being required; (4) near-miss types (P63 vs P70, P82 vs P02, P19 vs P32, UNCOVERED vs P102). Document stance differed only for the GenAI Guidelines (A permit, B delegates); final is permit because the guidelines encourage GenAI use with conditions for all users and defer only the coursework rule. Sample syllabus statements on the CTE pages (journalism, business, nursing, English HNRS 190, engineering ME 208) are coded as policies because they state concrete rules, but they are CTE examples and not KU-wide rules; the HNRS 190 sample is from an honors course, not computing. Several CTE samples repeat across the two CTE pages and are coded once per document. School and computing layers: none found; course layer deferred.

documents.title: Maintaining academic integrity in the AI era
documents.summary: CTE guidance linking AI to Senate Rules misconduct, urging instructors to permit AI, to discuss rules with students, to avoid detectors, and to redesign assignments. Includes sample syllabus text and a teacher's letter.

documents.title: Building AI policies into your syllabus
tiers: AI treated as a professional tool
Example: engineering (allowed with citation and chatlog)
documents.summary: CTE page on writing syllabus AI policies with discipline examples (engineering, journalism, business, nursing, English) from restricted to professional-tool, and notes on defining misuse and detectors.

documents.unit: KU AI Taskforce / Office of Audit, Risk & Compliance
documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) Guidelines
documents.summary: Campus-wide GenAI principles for all users: definition of GenAI and AI, responsibility for outputs, verification, routine-assistance disclosure exemption, compliance with law and policy, data protection, research disclosure, and prohibited malware or spam uses. Only the course-specific clause is about teaching directly.

documents.title: Guidance for Students
documents.summary: Student-facing guidance: AI can help learning but must not replace the student's effort, students follow each instructor's rules, verify and own output, cite when required, protect privacy, and existing integrity rules still apply.

documents.unit: KU Artificial Intelligence (ai.ku.edu, university AI task force)
documents.title: Guidance for Instructors
documents.summary: University AI task force guidance that leaves AI use to instructors, suggests syllabus statements and integrity reminders, warns against AI detectors and points to CTE support. No ban or requirement is stated.

name: Kean University
notes: The standalone pages found by search (kean.edu/media/ai-chatgpt-expectations-and-guidance-teaching returns 404; kean.edu/ai-kean returns 'not authorized'; ctl.kean.edu AI pages redirect to a SharePoint login) are inaccessible. The manual quotes the Academic Integrity Policy's AI text, so the substance is captured. No school/college or computing-unit AI policy was found. Reconciled from two independent codings.

documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs (Instructional Faculty Academic Policy Manual; Academic Integrity Policy)
documents.title: Kean University Instructional Faculty Academic Policy Manual and Resource Guide, Fall 2025: Expectations of Generative AI
documents.date_or_term: Fall 2025 (AI text from the Academic Integrity Policy, Fall 2024 revision)
documents.summary: Kean's faculty manual reproduces the university's AI statement from its Academic Integrity Policy (Fall 2024). Each instructor sets AI rules in the syllabus, while universal rules apply everywhere: AI output is not original student work, must be cited where AI is allowed, and must be reviewed by students, with misuse handled as an integrity violation. The manual also advises faculty on how much AI to permit and how to handle suspected misuse.

name: Kennesaw State University
notes: No separate computing-department policy found; the CCSE FYE page is coded as school layer. The university policy defers to a Guidance Document that was not available. Repeated warning and credit text in the Required syllabus template is skipped as an exact repeat. One UNCOVERED unit: mandatory annual AI training with acknowledgement. Reconciled from coders A and B; the committee duty to communicate inventory review results was coded by neither coder and is not added.

documents.title: Kennesaw State University Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: A short institution-wide policy effective May 1, 2026 that sets ethical and security principles for AI-enabled tools, creates an AI Governance Committee to approve tools and maintain a separate Guidance Document, and requires annual AI training. It sets no rules for how students may use AI in coursework.

documents.title: Sample Syllabus Statements on AI Use
tiers: AI Use Allowed, but Not Required
documents.summary: A university teaching-office page encouraging faculty to publish an AI policy in each syllabus and offering three templates: prohibited, allowed but not required, and required. The allowed and required templates repeat the same warning, responsibility and credit language, which is coded once.

documents.unit: College of Computing and Software Engineering (CCSE), First Year Experience
documents.title: CCSE FYE Policies (Academic Misconduct: AI & Cheating)
documents.summary: The first-year programming page of the computing college says all labs, assignments, quizzes and tests must be written without AI, lists AI use as academic misconduct, and bans AI in exams with penalties up to an F. It applies to the FYE course sequence only.

name: Kent State University
notes: Kent State CS department page https://www.kent.edu/cs/academic-dishonesty (fetched as v2-kent-state-cs-dishonesty.txt) is a policy on collaboration in programming assignments and has no AI or GAI text, so it was not collected. Computing therefore counts as none-found, though the page does state the department's cooperation rules. The Kent news item about the policy revision (kent.edu/today/news/adding-ai-cheating-and-plagiarism-policy) is a news article and was not collected. The CTL faculty AI pages (kent.edu/ai/faculty) return 'Access denied'; search snippets say the CTL offers model syllabus language for AI prohibited / permitted / integrated, but the text was not retrieved. Reconciliation: non-AI hearing-panel mechanics (panel composition, annual training, eligibility to sit, recordings) found only by B were dropped; sanction, hearing and appeal rules that apply to GAI misuse via the cheating definition were kept.

documents.unit: University Policy Register (Office of General Counsel / Provost)

documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); revised to add generative AI
documents.summary: Kent State's administrative policy on student cheating and plagiarism, revised to add generative AI. GAI is defined, barred on exams and coursework unless the instructor expressly permits it, and added to the cheating and plagiarism definitions, with the general sanction, appeal and hearing procedures applying.

name: University of Kentucky
notes: Collect file records no school, computing or course documents for Kentucky (course layer deferred). Some anchors include footnote numbers run into the text by PDF extraction. The reference list at the end of the PDF is not coded. Reconciled from coder A (92 units) and coder B (97 units). List items about effective uses: students' items are coded informs (the text says AI 'has shown potential to be effective'), while both coders coded the parallel instructor items may and that agreed code was kept.

documents.unit: UK ADVANCE (Office of the Provost generative AI committee)
documents.title: UK ADVANCE 2025 Guidelines and Recommendations for Generative AI in Instructional Contexts
documents.summary: UK ADVANCE's 2025 guidelines do not set a university-wide AI rule for coursework. They explain AI's capabilities and risks, tell instructors how to write and communicate a course policy along a four-point spectrum, advise against AI detectors, and suggest assignment designs and instructor uses of AI.

name: Lafayette College
notes: Both coders found no accessible document. No document collected. The college-level source is the Provost-appointed working group's 'Informational Guide: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Lafayette Faculty and Staff Members' (about 41 pages, with sample course policies), linked from https://provost.lafayette.edu/policies-and-procedures and https://citls.lafayette.edu/2023/08/23/guidance-on-generative-ai/. It is a Google Doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1p1PNSIfc6mLQ5q2gt__InVsM6Wl18-TmD125cHZsL2k/edit) that requires a Google sign-in, so fetch_text.py (edit and export routes) got only the login page. The CITLS page 'Teaching and Generative AI: Curated Resources' (citls.lafayette.edu/?p=18373) is a resource list with no rules, and the provost page only links to the guide, so neither was collected. Search snippets say faculty voted that syllabi must include course-specific AI policies, but no official text was retrieved. No CS department AI policy was found; the Biology department's academic integrity statement mentions generative AI but is not a computing unit. The only known URL (CS150 syllabus, Wayback) is a course document and is deferred.

name: Lamar University
notes: No school-level or computing-unit AI policy found; course layer deferred in the collect file. The CST-hosted PDF is a revised version of the CTLE PDF (same origin); both coded in full as instructed. Uncovered units: AI-enabled phishing/deepfake security awareness (in both guidance docs) and instructors discussing AI ethics with students (coded once per document). No new types: the two UNCOVERED units (AI-enabled phishing and deepfake security caution, one per CTLE-derived document) are kept as UNCOVERED.

The Lamar samples cover prohibited use, permitted use with restrictions and cited output, and encouraged use of Copilot with attribution.

Overlaps heavily with the CST-hosted document, coded separately.

tiers: Prohibition of generative AI tool use

It leaves course rules to instructors with three sample syllabus tiers, and adds research guidance on authorship, disclosure and peer review.

name: Lehigh University
notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Five Coder B-only units in the advisory report were dropped as descriptive survey findings or the group's charge (not policy statements). documents.unit: AI at Lehigh (Provost / Library & Technology Services)
documents.title: Policies and Best Practices
documents.summary: Lehigh's AI policies-and-practices page sets no course-level AI rule. It reminds the community of existing data-classification and acceptable-use rules, tells students to follow instructors' course rules and the Student Code of Conduct, and gives best practices on checking output, citing AI, opting out of training and using approved tools.

documents.title: Report and Recommendations from Lehigh's Generative AI Advisory Group
documents.summary: A May 2025 advisory-group report that surveys faculty and staff AI use and makes five recommendations: department-led integration, AI-readiness for students, administrative adoption, shared infrastructure and training, and regular policy review. It is advisory and supports both AI adoption and non-use.

documents.title: Teaching at Lehigh: Policies, Guidance, and Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: A broad Provost page of teaching policies and syllabus statements. Its AI section is two sentences: Lehigh has no uniform AI policy, instructors set their own and state them clearly in syllabi.

name: Long Island University

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Acceptable Use Policy
documents.summary: IT policy for faculty and staff using generative AI in their YU work. It covers data input bans, accuracy and bias checks, disclosure, research use, vendors, training, monitoring and review. It is not about student coursework.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy: Resources (syllabus language)
documents.summary: Integrity-office resources page with four syllabus templates for AI use, advice on written and electronic assessments, and a Turn-it-in screening threshold. It says generative AI is not permitted in most classes unless explicitly allowed.

documents.title: Yeshiva University Undergraduate AI Policy
documents.summary: Undergraduate AI policy of the Provost's Office. It sets a five-level framework (UG 0 to UG 4), defaults every assignment to no AI, requires written disclosure above UG 0, and sets integrity, privacy, faculty-use, assessment and governance rules.
